assumptions: the epsilon-quantized membership-query model with binary utilities permitted
1/epsilon is integral and the preliminary counting regime m <= (1/epsilon)^(1-delta) holds for fixed delta>0
algorithms are correct on every instance
randomized algorithms are correct for every realization; only query count is random
claim: Every correct deterministic or randomized algorithm has worst-case expected query complexity Omega((n-min(n,m)) + (min(n,m)-1) log(1/epsilon)); for n=1, Omega(m) queries are necessary.
failure_conditions: a hard-family instance is not singleton feasible
the leaf count or binomial bound is wrong
dummy pruning, Kraft, or Yao obligations fail
the exhaustive single-agent minimax value differs from m
paper_anchors: Lemmas D1-D5 in the omitted proof
